about.title: About
about.bio: I'm an Electronics and Semiconductor Engineering student at Tecnológico de Monterrey. I design, build and fly rocket flight computers, from multilayer PCB design to lab bring-up, flight testing and failure analysis. Before university I spent three seasons in FIRST Robotics, going from technician to Mechanical Lead.

hero.title: IGNIS Flight Computer
hero.subtitle: Open-source rocket flight computer · Ignitia Rocket Lab · 2025 – Present
hero.status: v2.2 flown at LASC 2026 · v5 redesigned for turnkey assembly
hero.intro: Custom flight computer for student rocketry: it senses the flight, detects apogee in real time, fires the recovery charges, streams LoRa telemetry and logs every sample. Each revision was driven by findings from the one before it.
hero.role: Lead hardware designer — architecture, schematics, 4-layer PCB layout in Altium Designer, RF and power design, sourcing, bring-up and lab debugging.

revisions.title: Revisions

items.text: Fabricated; too large for the rocket, redesigned before assembly.
First assembled; bring-up found schematic errors.
Corrected revision; primary flight computer at LASC 2026.
Two units built; halted by part availability and a USB-C net error.
Sourcing-first, all-SMD, turnkey; Ø75 mm board. Planned for 2027.

revisions.earlierLead: v1 and v4 never flew. Both were stopped by problems found before flight, and what they taught shaped v2 and v5.

v2.title: v2 / v2.2 — Flight hardware
v2.lead: The first flight computer PCB I designed from scratch, built around an ESP32-S3 with LoRa telemetry, GPS, inertial and barometric sensing, onboard logging and two recovery channels. Designing it in Altium was only the first part: once v2 was assembled, testing the real hardware showed problems that weren't obvious on the schematic or layout.
changes: Removed the SHT40. Humidity wasn't useful for the avionics, and temperature already comes from the barometer.
Corrected the barometer's configuration on the I²C bus after finding how one of its interface pins had been handled in v2.
Fixed the footprint of the addressable RGB LEDs, which didn't match the real part.
Added hardware continuity LEDs to both recovery channels, giving an immediate visual check on the board without relying on firmware output.
v2.changesNote: None of these changes required rethinking the architecture. They are the details that only show up once a PCB stops being a design on a screen and becomes hardware on the bench.
v2.buildLead: We assembled it in-house with a laser-cut stencil, reflow oven and hot-air rework, then bench-tested it before flight.

flight.title: Flight at LASC 2026
flight.lead: IGNIS v2.2 flew as the primary flight computer at the Latin American Space Challenge 2026 in Brazil, where the team placed 9th of 25 in the Rocket Challenge 1 km category. I analyzed the test and competition flight logs with Python and pandas.
flight.latency: Barometric apogee-detection latency, measured from flight logs
flight.loss: Telemetry packet loss, traced and fixed with a dual-antenna ground station

failures.title: Failure analysis
failures.lead: Three problems found in bench and flight logs, and how each one changed the hardware or firmware.

items.title: Wrong pressure readings
items.symptom: Barometer read 497 hPa instead of ~830 hPa.
items.fix: Fixed in v2.2; v5 defines every strap pin.

items.title: IMU lost after impact
items.symptom: IMU data invalid for 12,970 log rows while the barometer on the same I²C bus kept working.
items.fix: Address pin defined in the v5 design.

items.title: False liftoff in testing
items.symptom: A 40 ms debounce let hand movement trigger "boost".
items.cause: Debounce too short for real handling.
items.fix: 250 ms debounce plus a 30 m minimum-altitude interlock before any deployment.

v5.title: v5 — Designed for manufacturing
v5.lead: After component-availability problems stopped v4, I redesigned v5 around sourcing first: stock and lifecycle were checked before layout, and the board was prepared for turnkey SMT assembly at JLCPCB so it can be produced again without depending on its original designer.

stats.label: BOM lines also stocked by a Mexican distributor for local repair
Circular board mounted across the airframe

points: Alternate parts selected for the IMU and barometer.
Mounting the board across the airframe instead of along it shortens the avionics bay enough to fit the team's smallest rocket.
A complete manufacturing package for repeatable production.

platform.title: Across every revision
hardware: 4-layer stackup with a dedicated ground reference for the RF microstrip
Via-in-pad thermal pad under the MCU
Opto-isolated MOSFET pyro drivers with continuity sensing
firmware: I defined the firmware requirements (C++) and validated each flight-software change through bench and flight testing.
8-state flight state machine, barometric apogee detection, safety interlocks, LoRa telemetry and SD logging.
Python/PySide6 ground station with live charts, CSV logging and dual-antenna diversity receivers.

hero.title: LASC 2026 CanSat
hero.role: Satellite Challenge · Mission Leader · Ignitia Rocket Lab
hero.result: of 50 teams in the CanSat Satellite Challenge at the Latin American Space Challenge 2026 in Brazil.

points: I led the team's CanSat mission, providing technical direction and supervision.
The avionics are a simplified derivative of IGNIS, with added sensors that measure the vibration environment affecting the rocket's flight.
It transmits over LoRa telemetry and has its own parachute recovery, independent of the rocket.
